concerns.text: The plan applies segmented (piecewise) linear regression to the raw turn‑count data to locate a “tipping point” depth, but the turn‑count variable is right‑censored for runs that hit the turn limit. Performing ordinary piecewise regression on censored data ignores the censoring mechanism and can yield biased breakpoint estimates. The methodology should either (a) use a censored‑data‑aware piecewise survival model (e.g., a piecewise Cox model) or (b) restrict the regression to uncensored observations and report the resulting selection bias.

Cox proportional‑hazards regression is employed without any diagnostic check for the proportional‑hazards assumption (e.g., Schoenfeld residuals). If the hazard ratio for nesting_depth or branching_factor varies over time, the Cox model’s estimates become invalid. The plan should include a verification step and, if the assumption fails, consider alternative survival models (e.g., accelerated failure‑time or time‑varying coefficients).
